text:
Yes. I found several Texas providers who specifically mention **emetophobia** and/or use **exposure therapy/Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP)**:

- **Kimberly Wilson, LPC — Plano / telehealth statewide**  
  Explicitly lists emetophobia among her specialties and uses ERP for OCD-related conditions, phobias, and anxiety. She works with children, teens, and adults via telehealth across Texas. ([psychologytoday.com](https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/therapists/kimberly-wilson-plano-tx/933370?utm_source=openai))

- **Erikalin Ashton, PsyD — Austin / teletherapy across Texas**  
  Reports treating emetophobia and using ERP and CBT; her practice focuses heavily on OCD and anxiety disorders. Her listing says she provides teletherapy to adults in Texas. ([hoarding.iocdf.org](https://hoarding.iocdf.org/providers/ashton-erikalin/?utm_source=openai))

- **Bethany Bosier, LPC — virtual care in Texas**  
  Lists emetophobia among the conditions treated through CalmOCD and offers ERP for OCD and related anxiety conditions. CalmOCD treats clients age 5 and older. ([calmocd.com](https://www.calmocd.com/therapist/bethany-bosier?utm_source=openai))

- **Marina Zhukova, PhD — Houston / U.T. Health Science Center**  
  Lists emetophobia and exposure therapy among her specialties and appears especially relevant for children and adolescents. ([findyourtherapist.adaa.org](https://findyourtherapist.adaa.org/people/marina-zhukova?utm_source=openai))

- **Baylor College of Medicine OCD Program — Houston**  
  Offers ERP for OCD and related disorders; you could ask whether they treat emetophobia specifically and whether they have outpatient or telehealth options. ([iocdf.org](https://iocdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/Baylor-College-of-Medicine-OCD-Program-.pdf?utm_source=openai))

When contacting a provider, ask:

> “Do you have direct experience treating emetophobia—not just general anxiety—and do you create a gradual exposure hierarchy using CBT/ERP?”

Exposure for emetophobia should generally be **gradual and therapist-guided**; it does not necessarily mean being forced to vomit or immediately view the most upsetting material. Availability, fees, insurance, and age requirements should be confirmed directly with the provider.
